subject: Re: BYO key delegation and split-network keyflow - design review
messages:
From: Paul Reynolds <paul@enterprisecorp.com>

Subject: BYO key delegation and split-network keyflow - kickoff

Thanks Stephanie — following our security review, I wanted to kick off a quick sync on the BYOK architecture we discussed. High-level asks from EnterpriseCorp:

- We must retain HSM custody for root signing keys on-prem.
- Redwood runtime needs ability to request ephemeral unseal tokens for shard-level keys during model serving windows.
- EnterpriseCorp requires documented emergency zeroize and escrow access process.

I've attached our initial network diagram (network-diagram-v2.pdf) and a short checklist for the HSM operator. Can you confirm what latency we should expect for the HSM roundtrip and how the split-network flow (control plane inside customer VPC, operator tasks across an interconnect) will work?

Paul
Director, Platform Security
EnterpriseCorp

Attachments: network-diagram-v2.pdf (application/pdf - 1.2MB)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example>
To: Paul Reynolds <paul@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO key delegation and split-network keyflow - kickoff

Paul — appreciated, and thanks for the diagram. Quick answers up front, then a proposed small set of design options for review: 

Summary answers:
- Expected HSM roundtrip: 60-120ms typical for a direct VPC peering path; if routed over a customer-managed MPLS or VPN appliance expect 150-300ms. We measure median + p95 per hardware and network path; we'll include perf profiling during the POC.
- Split-network flow: recommended pattern is a three-tier key model:
  1) Root keys: held in-customer HSM (no Redwood copy).
  2) Tenant signing keys: sealed and escrowed; Redwood can request ephemeral unseal attestation via customer operator approval workflow.
  3) Ephemeral serving keys: generated transiently by Redwood inside the private runtime, signed by tenant signing keys via remote HSM RPC.

Design options (tradeoffs):
A) Direct HSM RPC (low operational complexity): Redwood runtime calls customer HSM (mutual TLS) for signing/unseal. Pro: simpler, lower latency. Con: requires opening inbound to on-prem HSM endpoint or strong peering.

B) Operator-mediated challenge (high assurance): Redwood requests an ephemeral unseal token; operator (customer-side) reviews context and approves. Pro: strongest human-in-the-loop control. Con: added operator latency + throughput limits.

C) Split-escrow + threshold proxy (mixed): Keys split across customer HSM and Redwood escrow HSM using threshold signing (k-of-n). Pro: avoids direct single HSM dependence, allows automatic failover. Con: requires cross-organization key ceremony and legal controls.

Action items for the POC:
- Redwood to run latency matrix against customer's proposed interconnect (Stef/Infra).
- Draft operator approval workflow and SLA (Marissa).
- Security policy draft for escrow and emergency zeroize (Karthik).

I'll attach a draft SCP we can iterate on and a checklist for operator access. Can Marissa and Karthik weigh in on preferred default and whether we should prioritize A (speed) or B (control) for the POC?

Thanks — S.
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
Attachments: hsm-operator-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>

Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO key delegation and split-network keyflow - kickoff

Agreed with Stephanie's summary. A few practical notes from ops based on our Dedicated and Private rollouts: 

- If customer picks option A (direct RPC), we strongly recommend a NAT + service endpoint model instead of opening arbitrary inbound ports. Use a TLS-terminating bastion with mTLS using a client cert deriving from the customer's KMS operator CA.
- For option B (operator-mediated): implement a time-limited approval token and rate limits. We should pre-generate a proof of intent payload that the operator signs; that helps with audit logging and rollback.
- For option C (threshold): we need a 3-party ceremony template and a custody agreement. This is doable for larger customers but will add 4-6 weeks to legal/ops.

Operational constraints to call out explicitly for the POC:
- Rotation cadence: tenant signing keys — recommend quarterly with automated rewrap to avoid long-lived symmetric keys in runtime.
- Emergency zeroize: define a playbook with steps, TTR, and contact list. Kimberly can own the audit evidence template.
- Telemetry: Redwood runtime will emit token-level traces but not key material. We'll provide redacted audit logs to customer.

I'll add these items into the Drive doc and update the operator checklist. Proposed default for POC: Option A with an operator approval fallback (A+B hybrid). Lower ramp time and meets customer's control requirement with minimal latency hit.

-Marissa
Senior Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

Paul/Team — thanks for the engagement. A couple of clarifications and a small ask before we start the POC: 

Clarifications:
- Audit evidence: we'll produce event-level audit logs (sign/verify/unseal requests) with request IDs and SHA256 digests of the signed payload. No key material leaves the HSM.
- Latency tolerance: for synchronous signing (latency-sensitive paths) threshold signing will add ~50-150ms depending on proxying. If EnterpriseCorp's SLA requires sub-100ms p95, we should test direct RPC over peering.

POC ask (simple): please provide a single representative HSM host behind your interconnect for a 2-week window with a test-only signing endpoint and a read-only operator account. We'll run a batch of 1k signing requests across different sizes to measure tails. We also need the contact for the operator who will sign the approval tokens during business hours (name + email + mobile).

Next steps summary (I'll own implementation tasks):
- Redwood infra to run latency matrix and load test (ETA 10 business days).
- Marissa to finalize operator checklist and approval-token format (ETA 3 business days).
- Kimberly to draft escrow/zeroize evidence template and retention boundaries (ETA 5 business days).
- Paul/EnterpriseCorp to provide test HSM endpoint and operator contact (please reply inline).

I'll attach the current policy draft to the Drive folder.

Thanks — Karthik
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
